# #680 — [cutover-blocker] Spool quarantine is a permanent SILENT drop — 15 turns + ~44 lifecycle events abandoned, count=0 in DB, spool_pending reads 0

State: OPEN
Author: rodaddy
Labels: none

Updated: 2026-08-09T04:35:27Z

---

Found by two independent pre-cutover capture audits (2026-08-09) and CONFIRMED by the controller directly this session (DB query + disk read). The single most serious finding of the sweep: the capture pipeline is silently dropping data RIGHT NOW, proven on disk, not theorized.

## Mechanism
The spool is presented as the durability backstop (deliver.py:6-7). It is NOT unconditional: after DEFAULT_QUARANTINE_THRESHOLD=5 consecutive replay failures (python/openbrain-memory/src/openbrain_memory/spool.py:42), a unit is moved to a sidecar file and ABANDONED.

## Confirmed on disk + DB (controller, this session)
Quarantine file ~/.local/state/openbrain-memory/claude-spool.jsonl.quarantine.jsonl holds, by operation:
- ingest_raw_turn: 1 unit / 15 turns (roles user:1, assistant:9, tool:5), quarantined 2026-07-30
- session_start: 22, session_wrap: 20, append_session_event: 2 — all consecutive_failures=5, abandoned
The 15 raw turn_uuids queried against ob_raw_turns: **present_in_db = 0**. Gone. The same session_ref has 1,819 other turns present, so the session looked healthy while these were lost forever.

## The observability gap (this is the defect class)
- spool_pending counts only object lines in the LIVE spool (outage.py:270-288). Quarantine is a DIFFERENT file, so pending reads 0 — the drop makes the counter go DOWN.
- Live /health right now: spool_pending:0, reason:"capture lane delivering".
- The observer hard-codes spoolPending:0, outageAnnouncements:0 (liveness-observer.ts:264-265), so the reader's spool_unannounced fault is STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE from the server.
- quarantined_count exists (spool.py:101) with ZERO consumers outside the spool module — computed, never read.

## Why this is a cutover blocker
On core01 this is the memory-durability guarantee. A quarantine drop is permanent, invisible in /health, and invisible to the liveness observer that is our cutover evidence. We would cut over believing "capture never drops a turn" (docs/decisions/capture-never-drops-a-turn.md) while it demonstrably does.

## Wanted
1. Surface quarantine in /health and the observer: spool_unannounced (or a new quarantined fault) must fire when quarantined_count>0. Wire quarantined_count to a reader.
2. Decide the quarantine policy: is abandon-after-5 ever acceptable for durable memory? If a unit can't deliver, it should stay pending + loud, not move to a silent sidecar. (Ties to #296 ordered-spool-replay + durability receipts, still open.)
3. A done-means check: force 5 replay failures, assert the turn is either still pending OR a fault is raised — never silently in a sidecar with pending=0.
4. Operationally: the 15 turns + lifecycle events already quarantined are lost; decide whether to attempt a manual replay of the sidecar before cutover.

Truth grammar: RUNNING — the drop is on disk and the absence is confirmed in the live DB this session.
